name: Browser extension | Notelet
tagline: Notes and to-dos for each page and each site, in Chrome's side panel or Firefox's sidebar.

keyPoints: Notes and to-dos attached to the current page or to its whole site, following tab switches.
Reorderable to-do lists, with completed items tucked away. Items can move between a page and its site.
Stored on the device or synced with the browser profile. No account, no servers, no tracking.
Fully usable with the keyboard and screen readers.
One codebase for Chrome and Firefox, built with Nutin.

popTagline: Built to keep notes about a page where they belong: next to it.

overview.mainContent: Notelet is a browser extension whose panel is a Nutin application mounted without the router. A background script follows the active tab, and the panel shows the notes and to-dos of that page and its site.
keyPoints: Chrome's side panel and Firefox's sidebar from one source: Firefox's manifest is derived from Chrome's at build time.
Addresses normalized before being used as keys (no fragment, no tracking parameters).
Switching between local and synced storage, with an item-by-item merge when sync is turned on.
Reproducible packages: the same sources give the same archive, byte for byte.

purpose.title: Purpose
keyPoints: To ship a product through store reviews, from permission justifications to a privacy policy.
To use Nutin outside of a classic website.
To build an accessible interface for a dense, keyboard-heavy tool.

constraints.title: Constraints
keyPoints: Minimal permissions: the active tab's address only, never page contents.
No network requests: data stays in the browser's storage.

choices.title: Faking browser APIs in tests
choices.mainContent: Application tests run against a fake of the extension APIs, which can also behave like Firefox: storage and tab logic is tested without a browser.

choices.title: A release pipeline with approval
choices.mainContent: CI builds, tests, packages and lints both extensions, and checks that a second build gives the same archive. A version tag creates the GitHub release, then store submissions wait for manual approval.
choices.after: Third-party actions are pinned to commit hashes and updated by Dependabot.

challenges.title: Concurrent windows
challenges.mainContent: Each window has its own panel, saving on its own: two windows changing the same list at the very same moment can lose one change.
challenges.after: Known limitations are documented rather than hidden.

challenges.title: Sync conflicts
challenges.mainContent: Browser sync keeps one entry per list, so the last write wins between two computers. Turning sync on merges lists item by item instead.

keyPoints: Publishing to stores is a project in itself: permissions, reviews, privacy.
Documenting known limitations is part of the product.
